title: Containment and Recovery Runbook — Customer Impact Incidents
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

This runbook describes a focused containment-and-recovery workflow for incidents that have measurable customer impact (errors, high latency, failed inference, or data loss risk). It is intentionally concise to support fast decision-making during the first 60–180 minutes of an incident. Use this document for: production API degradations, multi-customer failures, and partial platform outages that require immediate customer communication.

Scope
- Services in scope: Redwood API (hosted inference), Inference Router, Serving Runtime, KV Cache, Auth/Gatekeeper, Billing/Quotas.
- Out of scope: isolated developer environment failures, feature request regressions, or non-production test clusters.

When to invoke this runbook
- Customer reports or monitoring alerts indicate user-visible errors >= 1% of requests or sustained latency increases beyond SLO by 2x for > 5 minutes.
- Multiple customers report similar failures across regions.
- Automated canary checks fail for >= 2 consecutive runs.

Severity classification (quick reference)
| Severity | Customer impact example | Immediate actions |
|---|---|---|
| Sev-1 (Critical) | Platform-wide API 5xxs, serving runtime OOMs, sustained >50% increase in error rate | Trigger incident process, page on-call SRE and product lead, open status page incident |
| Sev-2 (High) | Single-region degradation affecting multiple customers, queued requests and high retries | Page primary on-call, consider regional failover, prepare customer comms |
| Sev-3 (Medium) | Reduced throughput for a subset of customers, degraded quality but not errors | Triage during business hours, schedule rollback or config change |
| Sev-4 (Low) | Non-customer-facing internal telemetry anomalies | Track as ticket, no immediate page |

Immediate containment (first 0–30 minutes)
1. Acknowledge and declare incident: the first responder must acknowledge the alert in PagerDuty and set incident severity. Document the incident channel (Slack #incident-<id>) and brief title.
2. Capture the facts: service(s) affected, region(s), start time, percentage of requests impacted, error codes, recent deploys. Attach logs & traces links.
3. Assign roles: Incident Lead (IL), Communications Lead (CL), On-call SRE, Product Owner (PO), and Customer Success Liaison (CSL). Create an incident roster in the channel message.
4. Containment actions (choose applicable):
   - Route traffic to healthy region or fallback model variant (Runtime -> Router: update routing policy).
   - Disable autoscaling surge to prevent OOM cascades (Cloud autoscaler policy: disable temporarily).
   - Apply circuit-breaker at the gateway for noisy clients (API Gateway: set 429 threshold = current RPS * 0.6).
   - Roll back the most recent commit if telemetry shows deploy correlation (use git tag and deployment automation to revert).
   - Clear KV cache selectively if cache poisoning or large keys are suspected (follow cache-eviction checklist).
5. Short-term mitigation goal: reduce customer-facing error rate by >= 50% or restore latency to within 2x SLO within 30 minutes.

Diagnostics (first 30–90 minutes)
- Check recent deploy window: `kubectl get deployments --namespace serving --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp -o wide` and link to CI/CD pipeline step.
- Review traces for p99 span increases and hot kernels (Perf dashboard: /dashboards/runtime-kernel-hotspots).
- Confirm KV cache hit ratios and eviction spikes.
- Verify GPU node health and OOM events in node-exporter logs.
- Run targeted synthetic request to reproduce with headers that enable verbose logs.

Customer communications
- Principles: be timely, factual, consistent, and set expectations. Avoid speculation about root cause in initial messages. Coordinate all customer-facing text through the Communications Lead.

Templates (copy & paste, customize):
Initial (within 30 minutes)
Subject: [Redwood] Incident: Service disruption affecting inference requests\Body: We are currently investigating an issue impacting Redwood hosted inference in [regions]. Some customers may see increased errors or latency. Our engineering team is actively working on containment and we will provide an update within 30 minutes. Incident ID: {INC_ID}. For real-time updates: {STATUS_PAGE_LINK}.

Periodic update (every 30–60 minutes)\Subject: [Redwood] Incident update: Investigation in progress (Incident {INC_ID})\Body: Current status: Engineering has identified [symptom], mitigation in progress (e.g., routing change / rollback). Impact: approximately {percent}% of requests affected in [regions]. Next update expected at {time}. If you need immediate assistance, contact your Customer Success rep or reply to this message.

Resolution (post-recovery)\Subject: [Redwood] Incident resolved — {INC_ID}\Body: The issue affecting inference requests in [regions] has been resolved as of {time}. Root cause analysis is underway; we will publish a postmortem within 72 hours. If you continue to experience issues, please open a support case.

Status page messaging (short forms)\- Investigating: We are investigating an issue affecting inference requests in [regions].\- Identified: We have identified a cause and are working on a mitigation.\- Monitoring: A mitigation has been deployed and we are monitoring for recovery.\- Resolved: The incident has been resolved. A postmortem will be published.

Status page severity mapping\- Sev-1: Major outage — show banner and subscribe option.
- Sev-2: Partial outage — show regional incident tile.
- Sev-3/4: Degraded performance — log only.

Rollback and rollback safety checklist
- Confirm no migrations or irreversible data writes in the failing deploy.
- Create a safety snapshot: increment DB replica or create volume snapshot (where applicable).
- Run smoke tests against the candidate rollback revision in staging and a Canary environment.
- Coordinate with Product and SRE for traffic switch plan and timing (include maintenance window if longer than 15 minutes).

Escalation and handoffs
- If containment goal is not met in 60 minutes, escalate to Head of SRE and VP of Product.
- If incident spans >4 hours and affects >3 enterprise customers, open a cross-functional war room and schedule hourly executive updates.
- Handoff to remediation team after service is stable for 60 minutes: IL creates a remediation ticket with owner, ETA, and checklist.

On-call rotations and expectations (operational notes)
- Primary on-call is responsible for first 30 minutes of containment and declaring incident severity. Secondary provides backup and monitors downstream systems.
- Escalation phone numbers and PD schedules are maintained in the on-call roster doc.
- Weekly rotation cadence (7-day primary) with a 48-hour overlap window at handoff for active incidents.
- During major incidents, suspend new feature deploys for the affected service until postmortem is complete.

Game day (exercise) plan — 3-hour template\1. Pre-brief (15 min): objectives, blast radius, measurable success criteria (restore errors to <1% within 45 minutes).\2. Fault injection (30 min): simulate high 5xx rate from a synthetic client; observe alerting and on-call reaction.\3. Containment exercise (45 min): enforce routing failover, run rollback, and execute customer comms.\4. Recovery validation (30 min): verify p95/p99 latency, run synthetic user journeys.\5. Retrospective (60 min): capture observations, update runbooks and monitoring thresholds.

Postmortem & RCA checklist\- Timeline: create a minute-by-minute timeline from first alert to final resolution.
- Impact: list affected customers, regions, and request volumes.
- Root cause hypothesis and evidence.
- Contributing factors (human, process, tooling).
- Action items: owner, priority, and target date.
- Quality gating: each action must have acceptance criteria and a verification plan.
- Publish: postmortem to internal page and a redacted customer-facing summary for affected customers.

Metrics and SLAs to include in postmortem\- Requests per minute (RPS) and error rate delta vs baseline.
- p50/p95/p99 latency shifts.
- Time to acknowledge (target < 5 min) and time to containment (target < 30 min).
- Number of customers impacted and top 3 affected customers.

Tooling and dashboards referenced\- PagerDuty incident playbook (link: PD_PLAYBOOK).
- Status page admin (link: STATUS_PAGE_ADMIN).
- Runtime perf dashboard (link: /dashboards/runtime).
- Canary/CI pipeline links (link: CI_PIPELINE).

Ownership and contacts
- Incident Lead: role assigned by on-call rotation — typically SRE on-call.
- Communications Lead: Customer Success manager or designated on-call for customer comms.
- Product Owner: product manager responsible for the affected API surface.
- Exec escalation: Head of SRE, VP Product.

Appendix: quick commands and snippets
- Redirect traffic to fallback region (example):
  - aws elbv2 modify-listener --listener-arn <arn> --default-actions '[{"Type":"forward","TargetGroupArn":"arn:aws:...:fallback"}]'
- Rollback deploy (example):
  - ./deployctl rollback --service serving-runtime --rev v2024.03.12
- Cache eviction example (Redis):
  - redis-cli -h cache.redwood.internal EVAL "return redis.call('FLUSHDB')" 0
